html:
A commuter railway in Istanbul, built from 2004 to 2013, that runs in a tunnel under the Bosphorus. It gave Europe and Asia their first rail link.

The idea of a rail tunnel under the strait was first put forward in 1860, under the Ottoman sultan Abdulmejid. Work finally began in 2004. The tunnel under the water is made of concrete sections sunk into a trench in the seabed, among the deepest of its kind. It was built to withstand earthquakes, as it lies near the North Anatolian Fault. Japanese lenders and builders took a large part.

Digging for the station at Yenikapı uncovered the Harbour of Theodosius of the Byzantine city, with dozens of shipwrecks, and delayed the work by years. It was one of the great archaeological finds in Istanbul.

The line opened on 29 October 2013, the 90th anniversary of the republic. With suburban lines on both sides it runs some 76 kilometres and carries hundreds of thousands of people a day.
sum: A commuter railway in Istanbul, built from 2004 to 2013, that runs in a tunnel under the Bosphorus. It gave Europe and Asia their first rail link.
